- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.38), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk reversal.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3%.
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3–5 days, consider mean reversion bias; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-forecast with a smoother transition.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to recent volatility; dampen forecast volatility by 10–20% relative to historical std.
